Rashi on Eruvin 15b:10:1.english: And there will not be breaches greater than the built [portion] - And even if they are small breaches, [each] less than ten [cubits].

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:11:1.english: Any breach that is [up to] ten [cubits] is permitted, because it is like an entrance - And [provided] that the standing [portion] is greater than them [the breaches].

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:11:2.hebrew: יתר מכאן אסורה - פרצה אחת אוסרת כל ההיקף, אפילו כולו עומד, כדמפרש בברייתא לקמן:
Rashi on Eruvin 15b:11:2.english: [If it is] greater than this, [it is] forbidden - A single breach renders the entire enclosure forbidden, even if [the rest of] it is entirely standing, as is explained in the baraita below.

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:12:1.english: [The] breached [portion equals the] standing [portion] - The entire perimeter is made like this.

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:13:1.hebrew: אגמריה רחמנא למשה - כדאמר בריש פירקין (עירובין דף ד.), מחיצות והלכותיהן הלכה למשה מסיני. שפודין וארוכות המטה פסולין לסכך בהן, לפי שכלים הן ומקבלין טומאה, ותנן (סוכה דף יא.): כל דבר המקבל טומאה אין מסככין בו:
Rashi on Eruvin 15b:13:1.english: The Merciful One taught Moses - As [the Gemara] said at the beginning of our chapter (Eruvin 4a): Partitions and their laws [are] a Halakhah to Moses from Sinai. Spits and the long rails of a bed are invalid to use as s'khakh, because they are utensils and are susceptible to ritual impurity; and we learned [in a mishna] (Sukkah 11a): Anything that is susceptible to ritual impurity, one may not use it as s'khakh.

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:17:1.english: Long [rails] - *Espondes* [in Old French, meaning boards along the long side of the bed].

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:17:2.hebrew: אם יש ריוח ביניהן כמותן - לסכך שם בסכך כשר. אלמא, פרוץ כעומד מותר, דהא הכא פסול ככשר הוא, ושרי. וקשיא נמי הא לרב הונא:
Rashi on Eruvin 15b:17:2.english: If there is space between them equal to them - [In order] to roof there with valid roofing. This implies that [where] the breached [portion] is equal to the standing [portion], it is permitted, for here the invalid [roofing] is equal to the valid [roofing], and it is permitted. And this also poses a difficulty to Rav Huna [bar Rav Yehoshua].

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:18:1.hebrew: בנכנס ויוצא - שיהא שפוד יכול ליכנס וליצא בריוח שבינתים, דהשתא הוי ריוח טפי משיעור שפוד, ואינו מצומצם:
Rashi on Eruvin 15b:18:1.english: With [a case where it] enters and exits - That a skewer can enter and exit in the space between them, so that now the space is greater than the measure of a skewer, and it is not exact.

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:19:1.hebrew: והא אפשר לצמצם - דקס"ד דהאי דקא מתרץ בנכנס ויוצא, הכי קמתרץ: דכל כמותן בנכנס ויוצא הוא, דאין דרך לצמצם. לכך פריך: והא אפשר לצמצם ולכוין שלא יהא לו ריוח יותר, ואנן כמותן תנן:
Rashi on Eruvin 15b:19:1.english: Isn’t it possible to be precise? - For [the Gemara] initially thought that the one who answered "where [a skewer] enters and exits" answered as follows: that any [case of] "equal to them" is [a case where it] enters and exits, because it is not common practice to be precise. Therefore, [the Gemara] objects: But isn’t it possible to be precise and calibrate [them] so that there will not be extra space, and [yet] we learned in the mishna, "equal to them"?

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:1:1.hebrew: ורבי מאיר מטהר - וטעמא דרבי מאיר מפרש במסכת סוכה בכולהו, משום דקסבר: כל מחיצה העומדת ברוח חיים אינה מחיצה:
Rashi on Eruvin 15b:1:1.english: And Rabbi Meir deems it pure - And Rabbi Meir's reason is explained in Tractate Sukkah regarding all of them: because he holds that any partition that stands by [means of] a living creature is not a [valid] partition.

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:20:1.hebrew: אמר ר' אמי - מתניתין בלא צמצם, אלא במעדיף ריוח יותר משיעור שפודין. וכמותן דקתני — כשיעור שפודין בנכנס ויוצא:
Rashi on Eruvin 15b:20:1.english: Rabbi Ami said - The mishna [is dealing with a case where] one did not make it exact, but rather where one adds space greater than the measure of the skewers. And that which it taught, 'equal to them' — [means] like the measure of the skewers [when] entering and exiting.

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:21:1.hebrew: אם היו - שפודין נתונין שתי, נותן לסכך כשר ערב, דאפילו לא העדיף הריוח, איכא סכך כשר טפי. דכיון דנותנו ערב, אי אפשר לעמוד אלא אם כן ראשו אחד מונח על השפוד מכאן, וראשו אחד מונח על השפוד מכאן:
Rashi on Eruvin 15b:21:1.english: If they were - [If the] skewers were placed lengthwise, he places valid roofing crosswise, for even if the space did not exceed [the skewers], there is more valid roofing. For since he places it crosswise, it cannot stay in place unless one of its ends rests on the skewer on this side and its other end rests on the skewer on that side.

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:2:1.hebrew: ולא גולל לקבר - כלומר, אם עשאו גולל, אין שם גולל חל עליו לטמא. גולל הוא כיסוי שנותנין דף על המת:
Rashi on Eruvin 15b:2:1.english: Nor the covering of a grave - That is to say, if one made it a golel, the status of a golel does not take effect upon it to impart ritual impurity. A golel is a cover, where they place a board over the corpse.

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:3:1.hebrew: ספר - וכתב לה ספר כריתות — ספר משמע קלף, כדכתיב: ואני כותב על הספר בדיו, והדר קרי ליה מגילה, כדכתיב (ירמיהו ל״ו:כ״ה): אחרי שרף [המלך] את המגילה:
Rashi on Eruvin 15b:3:1.english: A scroll - “And he write her a scroll of severance” (Deuteronomy 24:1) — “scroll” implies parchment, as it is written: “And I wrote upon the scroll with ink” (Jeremiah 36:18), and [Scripture] subsequently calls it a scroll [megillah, which is made of parchment], as it is written (Jeremiah 36:25): “After [the king] burned the scroll.”

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:3:2.hebrew: מניין לרבות כל דבר - שיכתוב הגט עליו. אי הוה כתיב וכתב לה כריתות בספר, הוה משמע מגילה. אבל השתא דכתיב ספר, האי ספר — ספירות דברים הוא, והכי משמע: וכתב לה דברי כריתות, אבל לא קבע לו מקום לכותבו, וממילא משמע: בכל מקום שירצה יכתבנו:
Rashi on Eruvin 15b:3:2.english: From where [is it derived] to include all objects - That he may write the bill of divorce upon it. Had it been written: “And he write her severance in a scroll [basefer],” it would imply a scroll. But now that it is written “a scroll [sefer],” this [word] “sefer” is a recounting of matters, and this is what it means: “And he write her words of severance,” but [the Torah] did not designate for him a place [surface] to write it, and it consequently implies: on whatever [surface] he wishes, he may write it.

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:5:1.hebrew: וכתב לה מאי דרשי ביה - כיון דספר לאו קלף משמע, ממילא הא לא קבע ליה קלף, ובכל דבר משמע. ולמה ליה למיכתב וכתב לרבות כל דבר? לכתוב: ונתן לה ספר כריתות:
Rashi on Eruvin 15b:5:1.english: “That he write her,” what do they derive from it? - Since “scroll” does not mean parchment, it automatically follows that [the verse] did not designate parchment for it, and it implies [that it may be written] on any material. And why did [the verse] need to write “and he write” to include any material? Let it [simply] write: “And he give her a scroll of severance”!

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:5:2.english: And she is not divorced by means of money - If he gave her money and said, “Be divorced with it.”

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:5:3.english: And she becomes another man's [wife] - This is betrothal.

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:5:4.english: Just as becoming [married is effected] with money - For we derive in Tractate Kiddushin (2a) [via the verbal analogy of] 'taking' [and] 'taking' from the field of Ephron.

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:6:1.english: From “a scroll of severance” - From [the fact] that “severance” is written adjacent to “scroll”.

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:7:1.hebrew: לדבר הכורת בינו לבינה - שלא יטיל תנאי בגט שיקשרם יחד, אלא דברי הבדלה יהו:
Rashi on Eruvin 15b:7:1.english: For a matter that severs between him and her - That he should not impose a condition in the bill of divorce that binds them together; rather, they must be words of separation.

Rashi on Eruvin 15b:7:2.hebrew: לעולם אין זה כריתות - דהא כל ימיה קשורה בו, שמחמתו היא נמנעת מלשתות יין, ותנאי זה תלוי והולך לעולם, ואין זה הבדלה. אבל מכאן ועד שלשים יום, הרי זה כריתות מיד, שהרי דברי הבדלה הן לסוף שלשים יום, ומותרת מיד לאיש אחר:
Rashi on Eruvin 15b:7:2.english: "Forever" — that is not severance - For all her days she is bound to him, since on his account she refrains from drinking wine, and this condition remains pending forever, and this is not a separation. However, [if the condition is] from now until thirty days, this is severance immediately, for they are words of separation at the end of thirty days, and she is permitted immediately to [marry] another man.

Tosafot on Eruvin 15b:12:1.hebrew: פרוץ כעומד - מכאן משמע דאפשר לצמצם, כדפירש' לעיל. ומפרק שני דחולין (ד' לח:), דמוקי קרא ד"תחת אמו" פרט ליתום: "זה פירש למיתה וזה פירש לחיים", ואם אי אפשר לצמצם, אמאי איצטריך למעוטי? מספיקא הייתי אוסר, דילמא מתה אמו והדר ילדתו והוה ליה יוצא דופן — אין לדקדק; דשבקינן לקרא דדחיק, ואיצטריך לשאם יבא אליהו ויאמר. ויש להביא ראיה מפרק בהמה המקשה (חולין דף ע), גבי בעיא דהלכו באיברים אחר הרוב, דמוקי לה כגון שיצא חציו ברוב אבר; ואם אי אפשר לצמצם, מאי קמיבעי ליה? ממה נפשך טעון קבורה, שמא יצא רובו:
Tosafot on Eruvin 15b:12:1.english: "The breached [segment] equals the standing [portion]" - From here it is implied that it is possible to be exact, as [we] explained earlier. And from the second chapter of Chullin (38b), which establishes the verse "under its mother" [Leviticus 22:27] to exclude an orphan [in the case where] this one separated for death and this one separated for life — and if it is impossible to be exact, why was it necessary to exclude [it]? Out of doubt I would prohibit [it], lest its mother died and then gave birth to it, and it would be a caesarean birth! — [from this] one cannot deduce [a proof], for we set the verse aside, as it is strained, and it was needed for [the case] where Elijah will come and say [that they occurred simultaneously]. But a proof can be brought from the chapter [entitled] Behemah HaMakshah (Chullin 70a) regarding the dilemma of whether one follows the majority with regard to limbs, where [the Gemara] establishes it [as referring to a case] such as where half of [the fetus] emerged including the majority of a limb; for if it is impossible to be exact, what is the dilemma? Whichever way you look at it, it requires burial, lest a majority emerged!

Tosafot on Eruvin 15b:19:1.hebrew: רש"י גריס והא אפשר לצמצם - פירוש: כיון דאפשר לצמצם, אית לן למימר "כמותו" דווקא קאמר. "אמר רבי אמי: במעדיף" — כלומר, מתניתין בלא צמצם, ו"כמותו" דקתני — ביוצא ונכנס. ותימה, דאין זה סוגיית הש"ס, דמשני: "במעדיף", ואינו חושש על קושייתו! ועוד קשה, דפי' בדרבא: אם היו נתונין שתי נותנן ערב, ואיכא סכך כשר טפי — ובפ"ק דסוכה (ד' ט:) תנן גבי העושה סוכתו תחת האילן: "אם היה הסיכוך הרבה מהן או שקצצן, כשירה", ומוקי לה בגמרא כשחבטן, ופ"ה שם: כשעירבן ואין ניכר איזהו פסול ואיזהו כשר. ועוד, דדוחק הוא דאמוראי מסקי אליבא דמ"ד פרוץ כעומד אסור, דלא קי"ל הכי. ועוד, דלא פריך בסמוך, כי מוקי נמי ביוצא ונכנס גבי שיירא: "והא אפשר לצמצם?", והתם ליכא לשנויי לרבא כי הכא. ונראה כגירסת ר"ח, דגריס: "והא אי אפשר לצמצם" — שיסתום כל האויר, ונמצא שאין הכשר מרובה על האויר ועל הפסול, או אפי' כמוהו; ופריך לכולי עלמא. ומשני ר' אמי: "במעדיף" — שבודאי יסתום כל האויר. ורבא אמר: "אפי' תימא שאינו מעדיף; אם היו נתונין שתי, נותנו ערב" — ואז נסתם כל האויר. אבל אין לפרש דדווקא כעניין זה אהני לרבא, ולא במעדיף — דגזר דילמא לא יעדיף; דבכל הספרים גרסי' בפ"ק דסוכה (ד' טו:): רבא אמר, אפי' תימא בשאינו מעדיף:
Tosafot on Eruvin 15b:19:1.english: Rashi reads: "Isn't it possible to be precise?" - Explanation: Since it is possible to be precise, we must say that [the mishna], when it taught "equal to them," meant precisely [equal]. "Rabbi Ami said: In [a case where one] extends [the roofing]" — that is to say: the mishna is [referring to a case where one] was not precise, and [the phrase] "equal to them" that it taught [means an amount sufficient for] entering and exiting. And this is astonishing, for this is not the [customary] style of the Talmud's discussions — that [an Amora] answers "In [a case where one] extends," and does not address [the questioner's] objection at all! Furthermore, it is difficult: for [Rashi] explained regarding Rava's [statement]: "If [the skewers] were placed lengthwise, he places [the valid roofing] crosswise" — and [thus] there is more valid roofing. Yet in the first chapter of Sukka (9b), we learned regarding one who makes his sukka beneath a tree: "If the [valid] roofing was more than them, or if he trimmed them, it is valid." And the Gemara establishes it [as referring to a case] where he beat them down, and Rashi explained there: [meaning] that he intermingled them, and it is not recognizable which is invalid and which is valid! And furthermore, it is forced [to say] that the Amoraim conclude [their discussion of the mishna] according to the one who holds that [when] the breached [portion] equals the standing [portion], it is forbidden — whereas we do not hold in accordance with this [view]! And furthermore, [the Gemara] does not ask nearby, when it also establishes [the enclosure around] a caravan (16b) as [having gaps of] "entering and exiting": "Isn't it possible to be precise?" — and there, Rava's answer cannot be applied as [it is applied] here! Therefore, the textual reading of Rabbeinu Chananel appears [correct], who reads: "Isn't it impossible to be precise [so that the valid roofing] blocks the entire airspace?" And thus it turns out that the valid [roofing] is not greater than the airspace and the invalid [roofing combined], or even equal to it; and [the Gemara thus] raises the objection according to everyone. And Rabbi Ami answers: "In [a case where one] extends [the valid roofing]" — so that it will certainly block all the airspace. And Rava said: You may even say that he does not extend [it; rather,] if [the skewers] were placed lengthwise, he places [the valid roofing] crosswise — and then all the airspace is blocked. However, one should not explain that only in this manner is it effective according to Rava, and not where one extends [it], because [Rava] decreed lest one not extend [it sufficiently] — for in all books we read in the first chapter of Sukka (15b): "Rava said: You may even say in a case where he does not extend [it]..."

Tosafot on Eruvin 15b:3:1.hebrew: תלמוד לומר וכתב לה מכל מקום - וא"ת: ואימא "וכתב לה" — כלל, "ספר" — פרט; אין בכלל אלא מה שבפרט: ספר — אין, מידי אחרינא — לא? וי"ל: "ונתן בידה" — חזר וכלל. אף על גב דלא מייתי בברייתא אלא כללא קמא, אין לחוש; דכה"ג איכא בקדושין בפ"ק (ד' כא:), דקתני בברייתא: "אין לי אלא מרצע, הסול והסירא מנין? ת"ל: 'ולקחת' — כל דבר הנקח ביד", ומשמע בתר הכי דמכלל ופרט וכלל דריש, דקאמר: "ונתת באזנו" — חזר וכלל:
Tosafot on Eruvin 15b:3:1.english: "The verse states: 'That he write her' — in any case" - And if you should say: But say [that] "that he write her" is a general statement [kelal], and "a scroll" is a specific detail [perat]; [and according to the rule that with] a general statement and a specific detail, there is nothing in the general statement except what is in the specific detail — a scroll, yes; anything else, no? And one can say: "And give it in her hand" returned and generalized [it]. Even though the baraita cites only the first general statement, there is no difficulty; for a similar case exists in Kiddushin, in the first chapter (21b), where it teaches in a baraita: "I have [derived] only an awl; from where is it derived to include the thorn [sol] and the brier [seira]? The verse states: 'And you shall take' — anything that is taken in the hand," and it is indicated afterward that he expounds [the verse] via a general statement, a specific detail, and a general statement [kelal u'ferat u'khelal], as [the Gemara] says: "'And you shall put [it] through his ear' — it returned and generalized."

Tosafot on Eruvin 15b:3:2.hebrew: מה ספר דבר שאין בו רוח חיים - בפ' בכל מערבין (לקמן עירובין ד' כז:), גבי מעשר שני [בבקר ובצאן], נקט צד של פרי מפרי וגדולי קרקע; ובפרק קמא דסוכה (ד' יא:), גבי חגיגה, נקט: "מה חגיגה דבר שאינו מקבל טומאה וגדולו מן הארץ" — הכל לפי מה שדומה לחכמים:
Tosafot on Eruvin 15b:3:2.english: "Just as a scroll is something that has no living spirit" - In the chapter Bakkol Me'arvin (below, Eruvin 27b), regarding second tithe [concerning the words: "For cattle and for sheep"], [the Gemara] took the aspect of "produce of produce and grown from the ground"; and in the first chapter of Sukkah (11b), regarding the festival offering, it took: "Just as the festival offering is something that does not contract ritual impurity and grows from the ground" — everything is according to what appears [fitting] to the Sages.

Tosafot on Eruvin 15b:4:1.hebrew: ורבנן האי וכתב לה מאי עבדי - אע"ג דאיצטריך למדרש וכתב לה לשמה, תרי וכתב לה כתיבי. והא דדרשינן בהמגרש (גיטין ד' פז.): "וכתב לה — ולא לה ולחברתה" — התם דריש מלה דוכתב דהכא:
Tosafot on Eruvin 15b:4:1.english: "And the Rabbis, what do they do with this 'and he writes for her'?" - Even though it was necessary to expound "and he writes for her" [to teach that a bill of divorce must be written] for her sake (lishmah), two [instances of] "and he writes for her" are written [in the Torah]. And that which we expound in [chapter] HaMegareish (Gittin 87a): "'And he writes for her' — and not for her and her fellow [wife]" — there, it expounds from the "for her" [lah] of the "and he writes" [ve-khatav] that is [discussed] here.

Tosafot on Eruvin 15b:5:1.hebrew: בכתיבה מתגרשת ולא בכסף - הך דרשה לא אתיא אלא לרבא, אבל לאביי נפקא ליה בפרק קמא דקדושין (ד' ה.) מסברא: דאין סניגור נעשה קטיגור. ומכל מקום, לאביי נמי איצטריך "וכתב" — בכתיבה מתגרשת ולא בחליצה. והא דדריש לה בריש קדושין (ד' ג:) דאינה יוצאה בחליצה מספר כורתה — ההיא דרשה כר' יוסי הגלילי, כדמשמע הכא; ונקט לה משום דהויא דרשה פשוטה טפי. וכן דרך הש"ס, כדאשכחן בהחובל (ב"ק ד' פז.) דמייתי קרא דבנעוריה בית אביה לגבי חבלה, ובריש קדושין (ד' ג:) קאמר דבהפרת נדרים הוא דכתיב. ובריש פרק אחד דיני ממונות (סנהדרין ד' לד:) דריש דראיית נגעים ביום מוביום הראות בו, דהיינו כאביי דפ"ק דמועד קטן (ד' ח.), ושביק דרשה דרבא דדריש התם מדכתיב: "לי" — ולא לאורי:
Tosafot on Eruvin 15b:5:1.english: "She is divorced by writing and not with money" - This exposition works only according to Rava; but according to Abaye, he derives it in the first chapter of Kiddushin (5a) from logical reasoning: that an advocate cannot become an accuser. And nevertheless, according to Abaye as well, "and he write" is necessary [to teach]: By writing she is divorced, and not through chalitzah. And as for that which [the Gemara] derives at the beginning of Kiddushin (3b), that she does not leave through chalitzah from "a scroll severs her" — that exposition is in accordance with Rabbi Yosei HaGelili, as is implied here; and [the Gemara in Kiddushin] cited it because it is a simpler exposition. And such is the way of the Talmud, as we find in [the chapter of] HaChovel (Bava Kamma 87a), which cites the verse: "In her youth, in her father’s house" [Numbers 30:17] regarding injury [compensation], whereas at the beginning of Kiddushin (3b) [the Gemara] states that it is written [only] concerning the annulment of vows. And at the beginning of the chapter [entitled] Echad Dinei Mamonot (Sanhedrin 34b), [the Gemara] derives that the examination of [tzaraat] afflictions [is conducted] by day from: "And on the day it appears on him" [Leviticus 13:14], which is in accordance with Abaye in the first chapter of Moed Katan (8a), and it leaves aside the exposition of Rava, who derives it there from that which is written: "To me" [Leviticus 14:35] — and not to my light [i.e., that inspection must be done by natural daylight, not by lamplight].

Tosafot on Eruvin 15b:7:1.hebrew: על מנת שלא תלכי לבית אביך - תימה: דהא אם מת אביה לא חשיב תו בית אביה, כדתניא בנדרים בהשותפין (ד' מו.): "קונם לביתך שאני נכנס, שדך שאני לוקח — מת או מכרו לאחר, מיד מותר". וי"ל, דבית אביה קרויים כל יוצאי חלציו, כדכתיב בתמר (בראשית ל״ח:י״א): "שבי אלמנה בית אביך", אע"ג דקראי מוכחי שכבר מת שם:
Tosafot on Eruvin 15b:7:1.english: "On condition that you not go to your father's house" - This is puzzling, for if her father dies, it is no longer considered her father's house, as it is taught in a baraita in Nedarim, in [chapter] HaShutafin (46a): "[Benefit from] your house is konam for me entering [it], [or benefit from] your field [is konam for me] purchasing [it] — [if the owner] died or sold it to another, [the vower] is immediately permitted." And one can say that all of his descendants are called "her father's house," as it is written concerning Tamar (Genesis 38:11): "Remain a widow in your father's house," even though the verses prove that Shem [her father] had already died.

Tosafot on Eruvin 15b:8:1.hebrew: ורבי יוסי הגלילי מכרת כריתות - קשה לר"י, דבגיטין בריש המגרש (גיטין ד' פג:) קאמר על רבנן דרבי אלעזר בן עזריה דכרת כריתות לא דרשי, ורבי יוסי הגלילי הוא בכלל הנהו רבנן. וי"ל, דהתם קאמר דלא דרשי לההיא דרשה, ולא בעי למימר דלא דרשי ליה כלל:
Tosafot on Eruvin 15b:8:1.english: And Rabbi Yosei HaGelili [derives it] from karet [and] keritut - This is difficult for the Ri, for in Gittin, at the beginning of HaMegareish (Gittin 83b), [the Gemara] says concerning the Rabbis [who disagree with] Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya that they do not expound karet [and] keritut, and Rabbi Yosei HaGelili is included among those Rabbis. And one can answer that there it means that they do not expound [it for] that [particular] exposition, and it does not mean to say that they do not expound it at all.
